title: Training Ground Atlas
subtitle: How the drill designer fits together — and why it's built this way
what: Training Ground is a local-first soccer drill designer and animator for one youth coach. A React SPA draws an SVG tactics board; drills live as single JSON files; a tiny Express server does file CRUD on 127.0.0.1:8123; exports turn the same board into PNG, MP4, GIF, narrated clips, and site bundles for the team's GitHub Pages site.
run: Double-click start-training-ground.bat (first run installs+builds). The app serves at http://127.0.0.1:8123 and this atlas at http://127.0.0.1:8123/atlas (or open docs/project_atlas/index.html straight from disk).

principles.name: One render path
principles.text: BoardSvg is a pure snapshot→SVG function. The editor mounts it live; PNG, MP4 and GIF exports rasterize the same component. The screen and the exports cannot disagree.

principles.name: Files are the database
principles.text: drills/*.json is the source of truth — human-readable, git-versioned, and writable by AI agents on a subscription instead of an API. The server is a deliberately dumb file layer; SQLite was evaluated and declined (see Decisions).

principles.name: The agent route is a first-class user
principles.text: Claude Code / Codex author drills by writing files. A watcher pushes SSE so they appear in the library within a second; rev stamps + a conflict ladder keep the app and agents from clobbering each other; the loader is forgiving (sparse steps, dropped unknowns).

principles.name: Meters everywhere
principles.text: 1 SVG unit = 1 meter, origin at the pitch's top-left, a 3m apron of legal staging space. Geometry IS the data model, so agent-written coordinates read like a coach's whiteboard.

principles.name: Deterministic exports
principles.text: Video/GIF render offline at a fixed timestep — no realtime capture, no dropped frames. The one exception is narrated takes, which intentionally record the live screen (voice + cursor are the point).

stats.label: Zero dependencies
stats.value: static HTML/CSS/JS, embedded data, file-open friendly

maintenance: Agents: when work changes components, dependencies, flows, or accepted decisions, edit docs/project_atlas/data/*.json and run `npm run atlas` to regenerate atlas-data.js. Bump the ?v= query in index.html if app.js/styles.css change. Keep entries short — the atlas orients, the code and docs/drill-authoring.md carry the detail.
